runtimePolicy.unknownValues: A name match does not verify native distribution, ecology, resource outputs, domestication eligibility or historical introduction.
runtimePolicy.identityPolicy: New taxon IDs use PLT, ANM, ALG or FNG prefixes; forms use FRM. Existing candidate/resource/technology IDs remain unchanged. Never reallocate IDs by sorting.
runtimePolicy.sourceInterpretation: Broad source groups have explicit non-exhaustive representative choices. These are design selections, not unique identifications of the original source or approved spawn lists.
runtimePolicy.resourceInheritance: Candidate resource bindings do not automatically transfer to every selected taxon or form.
runtimePolicy.lineagePolicy: Relations summarize evidence, not automatic gameplay transitions. Hybrid and introgression edges are not domestication edges. An extant species may only proxy an ancestral population.
runtimePolicy.varietyPolicy: Cultivar groups are not species, botanical varieties or named cultivars. No modern named cultivars or animal breeds are invented.
runtimePolicy.floraClassification: The plants folder includes source flora, including algae and lichenized fungi. Their scientific kingdom and ALG/FNG prefixes remain explicit.
runtimePolicy.gameplayIdentity: Gameplay identity is defined by the general plant/animal guide. Scientific names are optional background and never mandatory unlock requirements.

evidenceSources.title: GBIF taxonomic matching documentation
evidenceSources.supports: Taxon names and backbone matching; not evidence of domestication or geographic suitability.

evidenceSources.title: GBIF Catalogue of Life XR taxonomy
evidenceSources.supports: Alternative checklist for a species not resolved by the legacy backbone.

evidenceSources.title: Einkorn genomics sheds light on history of the oldest domesticated wheat
evidenceSources.supports: Wild and domestic einkorn relationship.

evidenceSources.title: Durum wheat genome highlights past domestication signatures and future improvement targets
evidenceSources.supports: Wild emmer, domestic emmer and durum relationships.

evidenceSources.title: Aegilops tauschii draft genome sequence reveals a gene repertoire for wheat adaptation
evidenceSources.supports: Tetraploid wheat and Aegilops contributions to bread wheat.

evidenceSources.title: A single domestication for maize shown by multilocus microsatellite genotyping
evidenceSources.supports: Parviglumis ancestry of maize; not a claim of no subsequent gene flow.

evidenceSources.title: Contributions of Zea mays subspecies mexicana haplotypes to modern maize
evidenceSources.supports: Mexicana introgression is distinct from initial domestication.

evidenceSources.title: A haplotype-based evolutionary history of barley domestication
evidenceSources.supports: Wild/cultivated barley and complex selection history.

evidenceSources.title: Six-rowed barley originated from a mutation in a homeodomain-leucine zipper I-class homeobox gene
evidenceSources.supports: Two-row/six-row morphological groups, not named modern cultivars.

evidenceSources.title: Molecular evidence for a single evolutionary origin of domesticated rice
evidenceSources.supports: Asian rice ancestry; exact domestication geography remains debated.

evidenceSources.title: The genome sequence of African rice and evidence for independent domestication
evidenceSources.supports: Barthii/glaberrima relationship, separate from Asian rice.

evidenceSources.title: Evidence on the origin of cassava: Phylogeography of Manihot esculenta
evidenceSources.supports: Wild esculenta ancestry, including flabellifolia.

evidenceSources.title: A chromosome-scale assembly reveals chromosomal aberrations and exchanges generating genetic diversity in Coffea arabica germplasm
evidenceSources.supports: Arabica hybrid ancestry; not a player breeding recipe.

evidenceSources.title: Evidence of long-term gene flow and selection during domestication from analyses of Eurasian wild and domestic pig genomes
evidenceSources.supports: Wild boar/pig relationship with continuing gene flow.

evidenceSources.title: Grey wolf genomic history reveals a dual ancestry of dogs
evidenceSources.supports: Ancient wolf ancestry; no living sampled wolf is asserted as the exact founding population.

evidenceSources.title: Rabbit genome analysis reveals a polygenic basis for phenotypic change during domestication
evidenceSources.supports: Wild/domestic rabbit relationship without a single domestication mutation.

evidenceSources.title: 863 genomes reveal the origin and domestication of chicken
evidenceSources.supports: Spadiceus contribution to chicken ancestry, with subsequent gene flow.

evidenceSources.title: Genetic analysis reveals the wild ancestors of the llama and the alpaca
evidenceSources.supports: Guanaco/llama and vicuna/alpaca affinities; hybridization caveat retained.

evidenceSources.title: Ancient DNA reveals the lost domestication history of South American camelids
evidenceSources.supports: Ancient introgression complicates simple camelid ancestry diagrams.

evidenceSources.title: Yak whole-genome resequencing reveals domestication signatures and prehistoric population expansions
evidenceSources.supports: Wild/domestic yak relationship.

evidenceSources.title: The origin of domestication genes in goats
evidenceSources.supports: Bezoar/managed goat ancestry, not ibex-to-goat progression.

evidenceSources.title: Whole-genome sequence analysis unveils different origins of European and Asiatic mouflon and domestication-related genes in sheep
evidenceSources.supports: Asiatic mouflon ancestral complex; taxon names vary by authority.

evidenceSources.title: The genomic natural history of the aurochs
evidenceSources.supports: Aurochs ancestry and admixture in cattle.

evidenceSources.title: Global genetic diversity, introgression, and evolutionary adaptation of indicine cattle revealed by whole genome sequencing
evidenceSources.supports: Taurine/indicine lineages are separate domestication branches, not upgrade levels.

evidenceSources.title: Whole Mitogenomes Reveal the History of Swamp Buffalo
evidenceSources.supports: Wild Asian buffalo ancestry of domestic buffalo.

evidenceSources.title: The origins and spread of domestic horses from the Western Eurasian steppes
evidenceSources.supports: Reject direct universal Przewalski-to-modern-domestic-horse ancestry.

evidenceSources.title: Whole-genome sequencing of 128 camels across Asia reveals origin and migration of domestic Bactrian camels
evidenceSources.supports: Keep wild and domestic Bactrian lineages distinct.

evidenceSources.title: Cenchrus americanus subsp. monodii synonymy
evidenceSources.supports: Taxonomic synonym of Cenchrus violaceus under Kew treatment; no automatic domestication edge.

reviewIssues.resolution: Review each selected taxon by region and habitat before enabling world generation.
The current research demo still uses wheat/maize aliases. Choose concrete taxa/forms before implementing species-specific progress migration.
Review source resource outputs at species/form level, including anatomical, sex and life-stage constraints.
Named historical cultivars and animal breeds require dedicated evidence; current forms and barley cultivar groups do not claim to enumerate them.
